tonight.headline: Likely alone against two Rams
body: You lead 102.02 to 80.36 and one game is left. Isaiah Likely is your last man. Panda Attack have Davante Adams and Harrison Mevis, both Rams, and need 21.7 more from their two than you get from your one.
There is nothing to do. Likely is already in the tight end slot, and Kyle Pitts — the only tight end who could replace him — played Sunday for 2.5 and is locked. Watch the game, not the app.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Puka Nacua did not practise Friday or Saturday and is questionable with hip and groin soreness on the Rams' own report. If he sits, Davante Adams is the Rams' number one receiver for a full game and the target share that would have gone to Nacua goes to the man Panda Attack are starting. Add a Mevis field-goal night in a game Los Angeles are expected to control and 21.7 is reachable.

case.label: The script that does not
case.body: Nacua plays through it. Sean McVay called it "some soreness" and left the status to be determined, which is the language of a game-time decision rather than a scratch. A healthy Nacua caps Adams around eight or nine targets and Likely only has to clear single digits.

case.label: Your own man
case.body: Likely is not on the Giants' Monday injury report — I read it on Giants.com and he is not listed. Jaxson Dart throws, and in Week 1 Likely went eight catches on eight targets for 78 yards and two scores with Malik Nabers active. Nabers is healthy again tonight, which is the one thing that could cut his route share.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nacua being ruled out inside 90 minutes of kickoff, which is when Los Angeles have to declare. Nothing you can act on either way — your lineup locked when Baltimore kicked off Sunday morning.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: When the week rolls · Tuesday morning your time
doFirst.title: Move Jalen Coker into the flex over Terry McLaurin
doFirst.subtitle: Washington lost Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow. Marcus Mariota throws to McLaurin in Week 3.

case.label: What changed this afternoon
case.body: Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow on the final play of the first half at Dallas. NFL.com reported Monday that Marcus Mariota starts Week 3 against Seattle and that Daniels has no return timeline, and will be out at least a week while he seeks specialist opinions. This is a quarterback change, not a box score.

case.label: Why the flex was held twice
case.body: This brief kept McLaurin over Coker through two losing weeks — Week 1 by 11.2, Week 2 by 7.6 as Coker went 14.6 to McLaurin's 7.0 — and held on route participation: 92.1% in Week 1, the highest on Washington, and nine targets at Dallas on Sunday for two catches and 50 yards. The instrument was right. It measured volume, and the volume is now attached to Marcus Mariota.

case.label: The receiver you are moving up
case.body: Coker led Carolina in receptions on Sunday: eight catches for 66 yards with Bryce Young. He is not a hot-week body — he is his own team's target earner, at 83.7% rostered, and his season projection of 202.4 already sits above McLaurin's 181.4. Carolina go to Cleveland in Week 3, which is not a soft draw, and I have not researched Cleveland against receivers.

case.label: The cost of being wrong
case.body: Nothing but a lineup slot. This is not a roster move, it spends no waiver priority and it is reversible next Tuesday. Chem's flex is RB/WR only, so both men are eligible and nothing else on the bench competes.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Washington name someone other than Mariota, or Daniels returns inside two weeks after the specialist visits. Or Cleveland hold Coker under five targets in Week 3 while Mariota still finds McLaurin eight or more times — that would say the route-share instrument beats the quarterback change and the flex goes back.

doFirst.title: Add Matthew Stafford, drop Kyle Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: Two Chem teams have no healthy quarterback. Stafford is 90.1% rostered nationally and free here.

case.label: The two buyers
case.body: Nicky Jam carry Jayden Daniels and no other quarterback; Daniels dislocated his elbow on Sunday and has no timeline. Footballers carry Caleb Williams and no other quarterback; Ben Johnson called him week-to-week with a hamstring and named Tyson Bagent the Week 3 starter. Two of the ten teams in this league need a starting quarterback before Sunday.

case.label: Why Pitts is the seat that pays
case.body: Atlanta are starting Cooper Rush. Michael Penix is out with an ACL and Tua Tagovailoa was doubtful with an oblique — Yahoo's Friday tracker had Stefanski naming Rush again. Pitts scored 2.5. Strategy also says not to carry a second startable tight end in Chem, where the flex is RB/WR only and a tight end cannot enter it, so Pitts is structurally dead weight behind Likely.

case.label: What this is not
case.body: It is not a points upgrade. Josh Allen scored 40.8 and starts every week you own him. The value is timing: Brock Purdy at 90.2% and Bo Nix at 83.6% sit on waivers until Wednesday 01:00 your time, and Stafford does not. For about 36 hours you would hold the only instantly-available starting quarterback in a ten-team league while two managers need one.

case.label: If the Higgins offer lands first
case.body: Pitts is also the piece in the trade below. If Bok-aneers accept before you unlock, this card is off — do not drop Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. to make room instead. Both held their own theses on Sunday and neither seat is open.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Footballers and Nicky Jam both land Purdy or Nix when waivers clear Wednesday, which leaves Stafford a dead seat — drop him next week at the cost of the seat and nothing else. Or another manager takes him before you unlock, which a ten-hour-old file cannot rule out.

whatWentWrong.lead: McLaurin 7.0, Coker 14.6 from your bench. That is 11.2 lost in Week 1 and 7.6 in Week 2, and the 13:10 brief held the call again on nine targets at Dallas.

case.body: The falsification clause written on 18 September was 'McLaurin draws fewer than six targets at Dallas while Coker clears eight again at Atlanta.' He drew nine. The clause did not fire, so the call was held and recorded as having been held through two losing weeks rather than quietly re-derived. That was the right process on the evidence available at 07:10 this morning.

case.label: What the evidence did not include

The injury happened Sunday afternoon but NFL.com only named Marcus Mariota the Week 3 starter on Monday, and the Washington Post report on the dislocation is dated 20 September. The 13:10 run had the injury; it did not have the starter announcement or the absence of a timeline.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +4.0 against your +1.4 — bigger than yours, and it goes in the message because that is what gets it read.

case.label: Why they might
case.body: Tucker Kraft is their only tight end and he scored 3.5 on Sunday. Pitts at 149.1 against Kraft's 145.1 is a slot they have not addressed all season. Recomputed on this afternoon's file with an optimal-lineup solver on both rosters: they gain 4.0, you gain 1.4.

case.label: Why it is a longshot, stated plainly
case.body: Higgins is in their starting WR slot, not on their bench — I checked the slot column, which is the check this brief has got wrong before. He also led Cincinnati in targets and yards on Sunday. And their actual WR1, Nico Collins, is out: Yahoo reported a Grade 1 hamstring strain suffered in Wednesday's practice. Asking for a starting receiver while their best one is hurt is the hardest version of this ask.

case.label: Why to send it anyway
case.body: Because Pitts costs you nothing to lose. He is already named as the drop in the Stafford card and he cannot enter your flex. The 1.4 understates the trade: the true comparison is Higgins against an empty roster spot, because the alternative use of Pitts is the waiver bin. A Grade 1 strain is the mild grade, so Collins may be back for Week 3, which is the version of their roster where this gets a reply.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They counter asking for Coker or Tuten, at which point the answer is no — you are not paying a starter for a WR3. Or Collins is ruled out again for Week 3, which closes their willingness entirely. Or the Stafford add fires first at unlock and Pitts is gone before a reply arrives, which is why this is sent tonight and not tomorrow.

trades.copyText: Hey — would you do Kyle Pitts for Tee Higgins? I know Higgins is a starter for you, so this is me asking rather than expecting. The logic: Tucker Kraft is your only TE and he put up 3.5 on Sunday, and Pitts projects a touch above him the rest of the way. With Nico Collins back you'd be four deep at receiver anyway. Straight up, no hurry — tell me if there's a version you'd rather do.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Still the best role story on this wire, and still without a seat to put him in.

case.label: The role is real and unchanged
case.body: Nine targets, seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown at New Orleans. Baltimore ruled Zay Flowers out with a hamstring on their own site, and were also missing Ja'Kobi Lane and Devontez Walker. Draft Sharks led their write-up with Bateman stepping into the absence. Nothing about that has moved since yesterday.

case.label: Why he keeps losing the seat
case.body: He would be your sixth receiver behind Jefferson, Garrett Wilson, Coker, McLaurin and Brian Thomas Jr., on a roster that starts two receivers and one RB/WR flex. Pitts's seat went to Stafford because a quarterback two managers want can be traded and a sixth receiver cannot.

case.label: How to take him instead
case.body: He clears waivers Wednesday 01:00 your time at 24.2% rostered, which is gettable even from priority rank 10 of 10. If you would rather hold the stash than the quarterback, fire this in place of the Stafford card — not in addition to it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Zay Flowers returning in Week 3 and Bateman's target share falling back under 15%, which closes the row at no cost. Or Baltimore reverting to the run — they were 37 carries to 25 attempts in Week 1 — which would say one nine-target game with two receivers out was game script.

doNotChase.name: Evan McPherson
doNotChase.lead: I told you to claim him nine hours ago. I was wrong, and the reason is that I read a rank instead of a projection.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Draft Sharks Week 3: McPherson 7th at Pittsburgh, 8.8 projected. Tyler Loop 17th at Dallas, 8.6 projected. The gain is 0.2 points. The ten-place rank gap is compression, not distance — ranks 4 through 20 on that board span 9.1 down to 8.4.

case.label: What it would cost
case.body: A waiver claim filed from priority 10 of 10 and a roster move, to gain two tenths of a point. Strategy says do not propose a move worth under a point, and says in as many words that a stream gaining 0.3 costs a roster move for nothing. This morning's card failed its own standing rule.

case.label: The argument I under-weighted
case.body: The card's own falsification clause said the strongest argument against it was that Dallas's kicker is ranked 1st for the same Baltimore game. Brandon Aubrey is 1st at 10.3. A board that likes the Cowboys' kicker most in the league is reading that game as high-scoring, which raises Loop's ceiling rather than lowering it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop missing again in Week 3 while Baltimore's implied total falls, or a genuine top-five kicker reaching free agency. Not a claim on a two-tenths edge.

doNotChase.name: Cairo Santos
doNotChase.lead: The best kicker on this wire for Week 3, and still not worth the claim from last priority.

case.label: The comparison, reported either way
case.body: Draft Sharks Week 3: Pineiro 4th at 9.0, Santos 6th at 9.1, McPherson 7th at 8.8, Loop 17th at 8.6. Santos is the best available at 43.9% rostered. The honest gain over Loop is 0.5 points.

case.label: Why it still does not fire
case.body: He is on WAIVERS, not free, and your priority is 10 of 10. A kicker at 43.9% rostered in a league where two teams just lost their quarterback is a plausible filing for somebody else, and losing a contested claim costs you the week's claim for nothing. Half a point is not worth finding out.

case.label: The Chicago caveat
case.body: Santos's 9.1 is built on Chicago hosting Philadelphia on Monday night. Caleb Williams is week-to-week with a hamstring and Tyson Bagent starts. A backup quarterback against the Eagles is a script that produces field goals, which helps a kicker, or produces nothing at all, which does not. The board predates the Bagent announcement.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Santos reaching free agency after Wednesday, at which point he is a costless swap and the answer changes. Or Loop finishing outside the top twenty again in Week 3.
